name: ACS770LCB-100U-PFF-T
title: ACS770xCB: Hall-effect linear current sensor, 50 A to 200 A, with 100 µΩ isolated primary conductor
summary: A Hall-effect current sensor in a five-pin through-hole package: the measured current runs through a thick copper path between terminals 4 and 5 (100 µΩ typical), and a factory-trimmed Hall IC beside it puts out a voltage proportional to that current. Bidirectional versions sit at VCC/2 with no current; unidirectional versions sit at 0.5 V. The primary path is isolated from the three signal pins (4800 VRMS withstand), runs from a single 4.5 V to 5.5 V supply and has 120 kHz bandwidth. Ranges are 50, 100, 150 and 200 A; the temperature letter (L, K, E) sets the operating range.
key_figures: 80 to 10 mV/A by range; ACS770LCB-100U 40 mV/A
4800 VRMS for 60 s; 1358 VPK basic working voltage

notes: ACS770 + temperature letter (L, K or E) + CB package + current range and B (bidirectional) or U (unidirectional) + leadform. Leadform PFF has both the current terminals and the signal pins formed; PSF has straight terminals and formed signal pins; PSS has both straight. Other leadforms can be had in qualifying volumes.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensed current passes through the part from IP+ to IP-, isolated from the low-voltage side. The 5 V supply reaches VCC with a 0.1 µF bypass to ground. The output leaves VIOUT through RF, with CF from the output node to ground, an RC low-pass that trims noise; RF and CF are chosen for the application.

equations.name: Nonlinearity
equations.expr: ELINpos = 100 (%) × {1 - (SensIPOS2 / SensIPOS1)}; ELINneg = 100 (%) × {1 - (SensINEG2 / SensINEG1)}; ELIN = max(ELINpos, ELINneg)
equations.note: In the performance tables the two currents are full scale and half scale.

equations.name: Total output error
equations.expr: ETOT(IP) = (VIOUT(IP) - VIOUT_IDEAL(IP)) / (SensIDEAL × IP) × 100 (%); VIOUT_IDEAL(IP) = VIOUT(Q) + SensIDEAL × IP

operation.text: Current in the copper path makes a field that a low-hysteresis core gathers onto the Hall die; a chopper-stabilized BiCMOS Hall IC turns it into a voltage. Gain and offset are trimmed at the factory and corrected over temperature by piecewise-linear digital compensation, which leaves the analog output's bandwidth untouched.
Current flowing from terminal 4 (IP+) to terminal 5 (IP-) drives the output up; a bidirectional part goes above VCC/2.
An internal shield cuts capacitive coupling from the conductor to the die, so fast dV/dt on a high-side, high-voltage conductor causes little output ripple or offset shift.

The current terminals are electrically isolated from signal pins 1 to 3, so the part can sense high-side currents without other isolation. The heavy leadframe is oxygen-free copper, leads are 100% matte tin and the package holds no lead (Pb). AEC-Q100 qualified; UL file US-29755-UL.
Output change per ampere: the product of the magnetic circuit's G/A and the amplifier's mV/G. The amplifier gain is set at the factory for the range's half-scale current.

With no current the output is VCC/2 on bidirectional parts (2.5 V at 5 V supply) and 0.5 V on unidirectional parts at 5 V. Its spread comes from trim resolution, magnetic hysteresis and thermal drift. Electrical offset VOE is the departure from that ideal level from non-magnetic causes.
Remanence in the core leaves an offset, largest once a full-scale or overload current has driven the core into saturation; it depends mostly on the concentrator material.
Quiescent output and sensitivity both scale in proportion to VCC.
The worst-case gap between actual and ideal output, taken in four cases: zero current at 25 °C, zero current over temperature, full-scale current at 25 °C and full-scale current over temperature.

Power-on delay tPOD runs from VCC reaching VCC(min) until the output is within ±10% of its final value under an applied field; a further tTC is needed before the output is temperature compensated. Rise time tr is 10% to 90% of full-scale output. Response time is from the current reaching 80% of its final value to the output reaching 80%; propagation delay is the same at 20%. Eddy currents in the IC's ground plane slow tr and tRESPONSE.

While VCC rises the output is high impedance. Crossing VPORH starts the POR counter; the output leaves high impedance only after tPORR has passed and VCC is above VUVLOH, then goes to VCC/2 after tUVLOD. If VCC is still under VUVLOH when tPORR ends, the output waits for VUVLOH and then tUVLOD.

When VCC falls below VUVLOL a counter starts; if VCC has not come back above VUVLOL by the end of tUVLOE, the output is pulled close to GND. If VCC recovers above VUVLOL first, the output stays at VCC/2. Once locked out, VCC above VUVLOH releases the lock after tUVLOD.

Below VUVLOL the lockout counter runs; if VCC is still above VPORL when it ends, the output is pulled near GND, and it goes high impedance once VCC drops under VPORL. If VCC passes VPORL before the count ends, the output goes straight to high impedance. The POR and UVLO behaviour applies to unidirectional parts as well.
The trim EEPROM is checked with a Hamming code and corrected after power-up. An uncorrectable error puts the output in high impedance and the part stops responding to field.

The Hall signal is modulated so that offset and the field signal separate in frequency; demodulation returns the field signal to baseband and pushes the DC offset up to high frequency, where filtering removes it. A high-frequency sampling clock and sample-and-hold demodulation give stable quiescent output after temperature cycling and lower thermal noise.

The PCB reference pattern surrounds each current-terminal slot with a ring of through-holes. Creepage and clearance from current terminals to signal pins on the package are 7.25 mm. The thermal resistance figure uses 1400 mm2 of 4 oz copper on each side tied to the primary leadframe with thermal vias.
